title: Priority steward 1:1 — cross-functional roadmap alignment (draft)
content:
Context:
- Quick 1:1 between Product (Aanya), Eng (Marco), and Applied ML (Lina) to reconcile Q3 roadmap priorities for low-latency chat + embeddings flows that are showing regressive token-cost in the canary.
- I (Finn) acting as priority steward to surface tradeoffs, capture decisions, and coordinate concrete next steps.

Goals for this sync:
1) Decide whether to: (A) extend current canary and fix model quantization rollout (short-term), or (B) fallback to previous quantized variant and re-run perf/eval sweep (conservative).
2) Agree on a lightweight decision rubric (latency delta threshold, cost delta threshold, user-impact buckets) we can apply to future rollouts.
3) Assign owners and deadlines for triage actions (instrumentation, eval prompts, deployment changes).

Attendees:
- Aanya Patel (Product)
- Marco Chen (Infrastructure / Serving Runtime)
- Lina Rodrigues (Applied ML)
- Finn Gallagher (note-taker / priority steward)

Pre-meeting notes I shared:
- Short summary of canary: 10% traffic, observed +12% token cost on long-context chat (95th perc latency stable; median up ~8ms).
- Perf traces show more KV cache misses for sequences >2048.
- Eval set: customer-chat-long.json (50 prompts) shows slight drop in rollup quality (mean ROUGE -0.6).
- Hypothesis: quantization variant 4b-int8 causing subtle KV alignment issues at tail; runtime scheduling + batching amplifies cost for heavy-left-tailed seqs.

Meeting notes / conversation highlights:
- Aanya: user-facing ask is to keep latency SLOs for interactive chat; cost increase is tolerable short-term if we prevent regressions in quality. Wants clear rollback criteria.
- Marco: runtime telemetry points to two hotspots: (1) KV cache invalidation at model variant boundary, (2) batch shaper injecting more micro-batches for long sequences. Containers show slightly higher GPU memory churn with the new variant.
- Lina: model-level tests show quantization noise concentrated in attention softmax for long context; we can try small re-calibration (per-layer bias correction) before full rollback.
- Collective: we prefer short mitigation (A) if fixes are low-risk and can be validated within 48–72h, otherwise revert (B) and re-evaluate with expanded evals.

Decision (tentative):
- Go with A: attempt immediate mitigation + extended canary for 72 hours with tightened regressions checks. If any of the following triggers, we roll back to previous variant:
  * latency 95th percentile increases > 20% from baseline over 1h window
  * token cost per request increases > 15% sustained over 2h
  * quality metric (eval suite) drops by >1.0 (absolute) on mean metric or any critical prompt fails semantic check

Action items (owner — due date — acceptance criteria):
1) Lina — 2026-07-20 — run targeted per-layer calibration patch (branch: rd/quant-fix-kr) and produce micro-eval report comparing 50 prompts (baseline vs patched). Include per-sequence KV hit-rate.
2) Marco — 2026-07-19 — add a short-lived runtime probe to emit KV cache hit/miss histogram and batch-shaper micro-batch sizes; add a dashboard tile and alert when micro-batches for seq>2048 exceed 30% of traffic in 30m window.
3) Aanya — 2026-07-21 — draft rollback comms + customer-impact rubric; prepare brief for support to use if rollback triggers.
4) Finn — 2026-07-19 — run a quick audit of the eval prompts to surface any brittle prompts that could bias the quality signal; list 5 that should be excluded or re-written.
5) Marco & Lina — 2026-07-22 — run joint end-to-end canary with patched quantization and runtime probes; collect cost and quality metrics and reconvene.

Instrumentation checklist (quick):
- Emit: model_variant_id, kv_cache_hit, kv_cache_miss, batch_shape_size, gpu_mem_churn_rate, per-request token_cost_estimate.
- Ensure correlating trace id across runtime -> model -> eval harness.
- Add canary tag to requests so metrics are segregated.

Unresolved questions / risks:
- Does the per-layer calibration require a full model recompile? Lina thinks not, but build-time patching risk needs signoff from release-engineering.
- Some enterprise customers have pinned model hashes; rollback may require explicit coordination with dedicated/private customers. Need to track pinned list.
- If we extend canary beyond 72h (to collect more long-tail events), how will that affect cost and reliability guarantees to other customers? Need finance ops estimate.

Notes to self / things to follow up on (scratchy):
- Remind Lina to include a small synthetic that stresses long-left-tailed chat (sequence 4k warmup) in the micro-evals.
- Ask SRE to sanity-check alert thresholds (Marina or Tom).
- Double-check if any recent rollout infra changes (release-engineering) changed model-variant sticky routing.

Communication plan:
- If mitigation validates: short internal note + update to canary dashboard + status on #infra-canary (Aanya to post).
- If rollback: coordinated page update, support playbook, customer email draft.

Next checkpoint:
- 2026-07-22 10:00am PT (30m) — review canary metrics and decide: continue / rollback / widen. Falls on Marco to host and present dashboard.

Quick decision rubric draft (to iterate):
- Severity buckets: P0 (user-facing outage or >30% perf regression), P1 (noticeable QoL regression >15%), P2 (minor cost increase <15% with no QoL impact).
- For P0/P1 immediate rollback unless short mitigation verifiably fixes within 24h.

End of notes — the plan feels pragmatic: try low-risk model-level calibration + better telemetry. Keep rollback button primed.

- JIRA INF-1284 (canary cost regression)
